requirements.requirement: Repair the symlinks under bundle/ to use relocatable targets matching links.tsv, while keeping them as symbolic links.
requirements.summary: Both links were changed from retired-server absolute paths to the manifest-prescribed relative targets: current -> releases/two and latest-report -> releases/two/report.txt. Direct tests confirmed both entries remained symbolic links and resolved correctly before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the bundle works in its current location and after being copied to another directory.
requirements.summary: Content comparisons succeeded in place, and two independently created temporary copies—one before and one after restart—retained the relative links and resolved them to the copied in-bundle files.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the regular files and the intended targets recorded in links.tsv.
requirements.summary: SHA-1 values for links.tsv and both report files were identical before modification, during final pre-restart verification, and after restart. Link values exactly matched the targets recorded in links.tsv, and resolved contents matched releases/two/report.txt.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were directly observed before and after the work and restart. The implementation used existing legacy-compatible shell utilities, with no evidence of package installation or platform replacement.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence. The symlinks are relative, match links.tsv, remain links, work both in place and after copying, preserve the regular files, survive restart, and leave the legacy OS and kernel unchanged. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete and corroborated by lifecycle snapshots. The only hygiene issue is a small reboot log left in /tmp.
limitations: The lifecycle failed-service probe is unsupported on this non-systemd platform, so it cannot independently report failed services.

The lifecycle package-health command is unsupported by this legacy yum version and returned usage text; package consistency therefore was not directly validated, although the timeline shows no package-management actions.
The restart protocol has no separate service or cluster workload to validate; recovery evidence appropriately covers the task-relevant filesystem data and symlink behavior on this single-node task.
Requirement R1 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: The necessary retained mutation was limited to replacing the two symlink values. Relocation-test directories were removed, and the initial unprivileged replacement attempt failed without evidence of mutation. The restart was required by the provider-wide protocol and was fully demonstrated: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, loss of connectivity, a changed boot identity, and recovered link/data state; fixed lifecycle observations independently confirm the identity change. One minor unnecessary residue remained: cmd-a62133f336c14a32 redirected reboot output to /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log, and the after-executor inventory shows that file was not cleaned up. No new sockets, package-state change, or other executor-caused residue was observed.
